correctness.rationale: For every t>=2, the formal Euler ratio F_t/C_t is integral and has constant 1. For t=p^a its factorization H^{p^a}, H=E(x)^{p^a}/E(x^{p^a})=1+pV, gives coefficientwise divisibility by p^{a+1}. Frobenius modulo p^2 identifies the least nontrivial coefficient H at n=p^{a-1} as -p modulo p^2, and the lifting lemma yields difference coefficient -p^{a+1} modulo p^{a+2}. For non-prime-power t, Frobenius directly gives the first nonzero coefficient modulo each p|t at n=p^{2a} as -m^2. Because d_t(1)=-t^2, this excludes all other primes and yields exact integer gcd. p=2, a=1, arbitrary m and all boundary indices are included; calculations in verify.py are consistency checks, not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The closest primary work states modulo t for t=p^a and p^2 in the a=1 case, with the negative non-prime-power obstruction. It does not state the sharp p^{a+1} lift for all a>=2, exact gcd g(t), or first tight index p^{a-1}. The full historical 3-core paper treats coefficient zero sets, not common content. Searches of equivalent series formulations, published records, and related arithmetic classifications identified no dominating theorem. Residual risk of unindexed or general-formal-series equivalence is retained; search failure alone is not treated as proof of novelty.
residual_risks: Elementary power-series lifting is widely known; an existing general identity may imply the precise optimal modulus and first coefficient without naming either partition series.
Searchable research records and primary papers do not exhaust unindexed publications or independent unpublished proofs.
The p-power negative branch for non-prime-powers is already covered in Sharma and is not claimed as a distinct novelty.

value.rationale: The natural motivated invariant is the largest integer dividing every coefficient difference between the two canonical hook-length and t-core series, previously compared modulo t. An exact all-t gcd and optimal p^{a+1} modulus settle how far this known congruence lifts, and identifying the first sharp coefficient gives a structural obstruction independent of finite enumeration. The valuation grows by one more power than the source proves for a>=2, with precise optimality; not an arbitrary selected residue or isolated numerical gain. The non-prime-power branch completes the natural dichotomy and is credited to prior work.
